children: Shares of J.B. Hunt Transport Services fell after the company's finance chief said profit is expected to fall 5% to 10% in the current quarter.
The stock declined 11%, to $244, in premarket trading Wednesday. Through Tuesday's close, shares are up nearly 40% year to date.
Speaking at Morgan Stanley's Laguna Industrials Conference, J.B. Hunt CFO Brad Delco said late on Tuesday that higher costs are currently weighing on the logistics company's bottom line.
The higher costs stem from strong demand, he continued, which has prompted the company to ramp up hiring, implement sign-on bonuses and institute raises.

Costs tied to recruitment, advertising, onboarding and training are expected to be roughly $25 million higher in the third quarter than they were in the second quarter, Delco said. At the same time, higher gas prices are also pressuring earnings.
"We're sort of facing all of that right now," he said. "In light of these costs that are hitting us, we are expecting our Q2-to-Q3 earnings to actually drop 5% to 10%."
Looking further ahead, though, Delco said the near-term earnings hit will set J.B. Hunt up for longer-term growth.
